name: CRAFT
author: Hannu Rummukainen (for Black Legend Ltd)

provenance.from: Ultimate Amiga AMOS Factory, CRAFT archive, retrieved 2026-07-26.
provenance.note: Recovered rather than found. The archive ships no .Lib at all -- only a DMS disk image whose contents are an Installer and seven opaque Data blobs. Decompressing the DMS (xdms) and reading the disk gave those blobs, and Data0 turned out to be FOUR libraries and a length table. CORRECTED 2026-08-11: the eight bytes at its head are not a prefix to skip but `dc.w $3478,$3478,$163c,$1634` -- the sizes of the four executables that follow, which are CRAFT.Lib, AMOSPro_CRAFT.Lib, MusiCRAFT.Lib and AMOSPro_MusiCRAFT.Lib in that order. Only the first was ever being read, because parseAmosLibOld stops at the first code hunk, so a file vendored as AMOSPro_CRAFT.Lib was in fact the AMOS 1.3 build and MusiCRAFT was sitting in the same file the whole time. All four are split out now. This entry points at CRAFT.Lib because that is the build every routine address in this port's citations was read from; the AMOS Pro build is vendored beside it. Their token tables are identical, so one entry covers both, and the ONE behavioural difference found between them is =Amos Pro -- routine 204 is `moveq #0,d3` in the 1.3 build and `moveq #-1,d3` in the Pro one, which is the keyword working exactly as documented rather than the defect this port briefly recorded. The other five packed blobs are now unpacked too, by src/cli/craftx.ts over src/amiga/solaris.ts -- the installer's container is [total:4] then [path\0][size:2] until the sizes add up, then one stream tagged \SOLARIS/, which is the in-house packer of the Finnish house that built the disk (Solaris_Logo.iff is on it). That decruncher was read out of the Installer, itself a compiled AMOS program, at hunk 1 $cce6..$cdac. Data6 is the only blob still unread: a music module, 'craft.jol' by Janne Leinonen. Everything vendored here can be reproduced from the archive by running craftx.
provenance.redistribution: Commercial: published by Black Legend Ltd. Redistribution terms unverified. Kept as a fixture for identification and reference only.

findings: 168 token entries, 138 of them named, over eight groups with little to do with each other: string handling (`up case$`, `flip case$`, `bw instr`, `str scramble$`), a LOGO turtle of 33 keywords driven either one at a time or by a command string through `Tr Exec`, a `dr *` directory scanner over AmigaDOS FileInfoBlocks, palettes held in memory banks, `Fr Mandelbrot` and `Fr Julia`, Workbench and CLI access, six memory queries, and hardware pokes down to `Y Beam` and `Guru Meditation`. It carries no library-name string at all, so nothing in it opens a library: whatever `Open Workbench` and `Sys Request` reach, they reach through a base AMOS already holds. Burton's AMOS Extensions List places it at slot 18, and the disk's own examples confirm the author -- 'Turtle spiral by Hannu Rummukainen' heads one of them. DOCUMENTATION EXISTS AND IS NOW READABLE: CRAFT_Help.AMOS is a hypertext reader by Janne Kalliola whose bank 1 holds 42,874 bytes of plain text, one entry per keyword with syntax and parameter ranges, indexed by 139 DATA statements naming 138 topics. It is where facts like Fr Julia's fixed point come from -- 'multiplying their real values by 8192'. Forty example programs came out of the same disk (fourteen Turtle, seven Fractals, five Colours, plus Token_List, Dir_List, Guru_Alert, Get_Preferences, Info&AvailMem, Priority&Multitasking), which for a library with no manual page per argument order is the better oracle of the two. NOTE THE HELP COVERS A COMPANION TOO: nine of its topics are an `St *` group -- st load, st play, st stop, st pause, st voice, st channel, st vumeter speed, st base, st version -- and none of those is in this token table. They belong to MusiCRAFT, a separate extension whose table stub survives in AMOSTools as AMOSPro_MusiCRAFT.Lib and whose binary is not held here; the disk's Sample_Demo, Toggle_Voice and Vumeter_Demo examples use it, not this library. Accessories/ holds two builds of four programs, AMOS 1.3 from Data1 and AMOS Pro from Data4, kept side by side with a .Data4 suffix -- the same two-build pattern Data0 turned out to use for the libraries themselves. PALETTE BANKS ARE UNDOCUMENTED IN THEIR ONE IMPORTANT DETAIL: the help describes the eleven keywords but never the record they share. Routines 84 and 94 have it, and status.ts cites the addresses -- the eight-byte bank name "Palettes", then 32 words per palette, and a word of $FFFF meaning ABSENT rather than black. That marker is core AMOS's own: PalRout skips $FFFF, which is what lets a masked palette be installed by handing over all 32 words and letting the gaps fall through, and it is why the help can promise that a deleted colour "won't be changed" on the way back in without ever saying how. The same rule cuts the other way twice, in ways nothing documents: a masked Pal To Bank DELETES the bank slots it excludes rather than leaving them, and a masked Pal Swap Bank erases the bank colours it did not swap, because its return leg is masked the same way as its outward one. Two more asymmetries, both between routines that look like a matched pair: =Pal Red admits colour registers 0..63 and reads 32..63 as Extra Half Brite (`lsr.w #1 / andi.w #$777`, and it never asks whether the screen IS half-brite) where Set Red stops at 32; and Pal To Bank's three-argument trampoline tests for AMOS's omitted-parameter marker and will create a bank, where its two-argument one does not and will not. THE TURTLE IS THE LARGEST GROUP AND THE ONLY ONE WITH ITS OWN LANGUAGE. Its 33 keywords sit on a 56-byte workspace =Tr Base hands out the address of, whose layout is documented nowhere: the heading is kept TWICE, as a 32-bit binary angle at $30 and as sine and MINUS cosine in sign-magnitude 16.16 at $34/$38, with two flag bits saying which of the pair is live and routines 106 and 109 converting one into the other only when somebody asks. All of it is fixed point -- a Taylor cosine, an integer Newton square root, a nine-term arcsine over a coefficient table -- and the position is 16.16 where only the integer half reaches the screen, so the rounding IS the behaviour and this port transcribes the registers rather than rewriting the mathematics. Tr Exec is a second front end onto the same routines: the table at $1c88 is twenty-two commands, each a Rbra onto the routine its keyword already uses, and only I/P (SetAPen and SetBPen) has no keyword behind it. FIVE DEFECTS came out of reading it, none of them in the manual. Tr Distance to the turtle's own position never returns, because its normalising loop waits for a carry that two zero deltas cannot produce. Tr Towards and Tr Distance both lose the interlace half of their aspect correction, because routine 105 tests d3 where it means d4 -- and the same eight instructions are written correctly inside routine 119. Tr Draw with the y left out moves to twice the current y instead of keeping it. Tr Set Home crosses its two omitted-parameter fallbacks. And Tr Home cannot reach a home with a negative coordinate, because it zero-extends the integer half on the way to the bounds check. There is also a one-nibble typo in the arcsine table, 63/1403 where the series wants 63/2816, too small to move a pixel. THE FRACTAL GROUP shares the same workspace at lower offsets and is entirely 16-bit fixed point with 8192 as one. The manual states the unit for the coordinates and the Julia constant; the iteration proves it, because a product of two coordinates carries 26 fractional bits and `asl.l #3 / swap` brings it back to thirteen, and the escape test compares that product against $10000000, which over 2^26 is four. The renderer clips the window against the screen's clip rectangle and the Fr Scan band and then recomputes the plane coordinate from whatever corner survived, so a band drawn in the middle of a picture lands on the pixels a whole one would. Two more defects here. Fr Step's two-argument form never stores its second number -- routine 142 writes d0 where it means d2 -- so both steps come from the first, and `Fr Step ,8` sets the y step to $ffff, sixty-four times the maximum the routine has just finished enforcing. And Fr Mandelbrot guards its iteration count with Rbls where Fr Julia uses Rbcs, so it refuses ONE as well as zero although the manual calls the two instructions identical. THE WORKBENCH AND SYSTEM GROUP is where the no-library claim above stops being an observation and becomes evidence. Not one of these eighteen keywords opens anything: IntuitionBase is read at -$18a6(a5), DOSBase at $620(a5) and ExecBase at absolute $4, all of them bases AMOS is already holding, and -$18a6 sits eight bytes from the -$18ae GfxBase the turtle draws through. Multi On and Multi Off are n/a rather than ported, for the reason JD's and MISC 1.0's identical pair already are: exec's Permit and Forbid over one task, with nothing in any of the three libraries that reads the nesting back. Sys Request's argument order comes off routine 187 and is not obvious from the syntax line -- the last TWO arguments are the gadget labels and the body lines are what is left, which is how three arguments make a one-line requester and seven a five-line one; its 'Retry' and 'Cancel' defaults are in the hunk at $3096 and $308e beside the topaz.font their IntuiTexts are drawn in. Guru Meditation is not a decoration either: `bset #$1f,d7` makes the number a DEADEND alert and the jump to exec's Alert never returns. THE TAIL brought two hardware registers into the memory map rather than short-cutting them: CIA-A port A at $bfe001 and POTGOR at $dff016, because =Hw Mouse Key's whole point is that it reads the silicon rather than asking the operating system -- "it works whether the AMOS screen is displayed or not" -- and a program that Peeks the same two addresses has to get the same answer the keyword does. The Gr trio pays for itself twice over: rp_FgPen, rp_BgPen and rp_AOlPen at $19, $1a and $1b confirm that -$18ca(a5) IS a RastPort, which is what makes the turtle's line-pattern write to $1f a slip rather than a design, since rp_linpatcnt is at $1e. =Amos Pro is a constant and there are two builds, one for each answer: routine 204 is `moveq #0,d3` in CRAFT.Lib and `moveq #-1,d3` in AMOSPro_CRAFT.Lib. It was briefly recorded here as a defect, which was this port reading the 1.3 build out of a file it had mislabelled.
notes: A grab-bag: string handling, a LOGO turtle, sprite and screen effects, file and memory utilities.
